{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABXcZG0g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhBAln4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 25, "title": "Add bounded UniformArrayNode and UniformArrayElementNode round-trip support", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 default loader/exporter support expression `ArrayNode`/`ArrayElementNode`, but do **not** support ordinary `UniformArrayNode` and `UniformArrayElementNode` instances. Three.js r186 uses these classes to read data arrays through uniform buffers (including native padding and per-render uploads). Their source arrays, element types, and node links are not fully reconstructible from generic `Node.serialize()` alone.

Add a deliberately constrained, data-only round trip for useful uniform arrays. Do not conflate an expression `ArrayNode` with an allocated `UniformArrayNode`, or assume the former's existing support covers the latter.

## Expected outcome

1. Audit installed Three.js r186 (recheck the current stable release during implementation): `UniformArrayNode`, `UniformArrayElementNode`, `BufferNode`, `ArrayElementNode`, `InputNode`, native setup/update/packing, `getSerializeChildren()`, and shader generation for GLSL/WGSL. Identify which state is constructor data versus generated runtime cache.
2. Extend the **existing** default exporter serializer and loader resolver with paired, narrowly scoped adapters:
   - Start with finite, nonempty arrays of ordinary numbers (`float`, `int`, `uint`), `Color` (`color`), and `Vector2`/`Vector3`/`Vector4` (`vec2`/`vec3`/`vec4`). Verify supported native type/packing combinations before accepting each; specify and document the exact allowlist.
   - Preserve array length, element type and element values as JSON data. Reconstruct real Three.js values and the native `UniformArrayNode` without serializing generated padded buffers or shader code. Handle native inferred versus explicit element type only where their meaning can be preserved.
   - Preserve `UniformArrayElementNode` links to the correct parent uniform array and its index node, with shared references and repeated round trips. Reuse existing graph traversal, child hydration and node-reference validation.
   - Let Three.js own uniform layout, padding, generation and `updateBuffer()`; retain its native render-update behavior without copying or reimplementing GPU upload/packing logic.
3. Clearly define snapshot semantics: the serialized array is material data at export time, **not** a persistent binding to the application's original array/object; imported arrays must remain mutable/updatable through native Three.js behavior.
4. Defer unsupported/ambiguous variants explicitly, with reasons and potential adapter paths. In particular, do not silently support app-installed callbacks, external mutable array identity, custom uniform groups, arbitrary buffer layouts/storage/compute, or `BufferAttributeNode`/`BufferNode` merely because this subset works. Matrices and other element types should be added **only** if r186 behavior and complete round-trip fidelity are verified; otherwise document their deferral.
5. Reject unsupported types, invalid sizes/ranges, mismatched value shapes/types, nonfinite values, unexpected fields/links, subclasses masquerading as built-ins, and app-defined update behavior **on export**. On import, any unknown/malformed operation, args, links, index references or array content must fail the **entire** TSL extension for that material and retain the ordinary glTF material unchanged. Do not partially publish the graph.
6. Keep Draft v2.0 and the existing NodeMaterial/material-property coexistence, materialType restoration and shared TSL singleton protections unchanged. No v1.0 compatibility, eval, executable code, or bespoke shader semantics.

## Context and reproduction

- [Draft v2.0 specification](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [r186 coverage matrix — CPU buffers and attributes](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md)
- [Exporter default serializer](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/defaultNodeSerializer.ts)
- [Loader default resolver](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/defaultNodeResolver.ts)
- [Integration tests](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)
- [Three.js r186 UniformArrayNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/UniformArrayNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 BufferNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/BufferNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 ArrayElementNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/utils/ArrayElementNode.js)
- Existing expression array coverage: #15; geometry/index coverage: #23.

Representative use case: `uniformArray([new Color(...), ...], 'color').element(instanceIndex)` in a material entrypoint. Currently the default plugins do not reconstruct this uniform-array family.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document the upstream audit, supported element types/forms, packing/update semantics, and exact excluded variants with reasons; use the current Three.js behavior rather than assumptions.
- [ ] Implement paired default exporter/loader support for the verified subset in the existing plugin structure, with validated constructor data and element-node links. Retain normal shared node identity, graph reuse and material entrypoints.
- [ ] Add real GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader integration tests for all supported element types (including boundary/inferred-vs-explicit cases), node identity/sharing, native index linkage (including `instanceIndex` where valid), and material property coexistence.
- [ ] Verify native array values, types, layout/padding and render-update behavior before/after import as far as the Node test harness permits. Compare native GLSL/WGSL shader generation where feasible and report unavailable backend/stage checks explicitly. Distinguish unbuilt vs built nodes where relevant.
- [ ] Add negative tests for malformed/empty arrays, incompatible values/types, invalid indices/links, unsupported callbacks, arbitrary groups/instances/buffers, and broken/unreachable graph definitions; verify **atomic** fallback against ordinary glTF material values/extensions.
- [ ] Update `docs/tsl-node-coverage.md` and affected loader/exporter READMEs to describe the verified subset and deferrals. Do not change the Draft v2.0 schema or bring back v1.0 support.
- [ ] Run and report the existing full demo test suite, loader and exporter builds, demo typecheck and build, and `git diff --check`; document actual results, warnings, and any skipped checks.

## Optional validation

Browser/WebGPU or WebGL visual smoke tests for uniform-array indexed colors and updates. If not run, state explicitly that Node-side shader generation does not prove GPU compilation or pixel correctness.

## Required post-merge verification

None. **Do not publish npm packages in this issue.** The maintainer performs `npm publish` manually in a separate release step. No version bump is requested here.
